For an additional amount for “National Guard Personnel, Army”, $1,304,000, for necessary expenses related to the consequences of Hurricane Katrina and other hurricanes of the 2005 season: Provided, That the amount provided under this heading 
is designated as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 402 of H. Con. Res. 95 (109th Congress), the concurrent resolution on the budget for fiscal year 2006.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriations provision that funds National Guard personnel expenses and designates the amount as an emergency requirement under a congressional budget resolution. No party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge any federal decision. The reference to a concurrent resolution is internal congressional budget procedure, which is not participation.
fable.s: For an additional amount for “National Guard Personnel, Army”, $1,304,000, for necessary expenses related to the consequences of Hurricane Katrina and other hurricanes of the 2005 season

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple appropriation of funds for specific expenses related to hurricane relief. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public comment periods, or requirements to consult with states or tribes mentioned in this text.
qwen_block.s: For an additional amount for “National Guard Personnel, Army”, $1,304,000, for necessary expenses related to the consequences of Hurricane Katrina and other hurricanes of the 2005 season

opus.w: This section only appropriates money for National Guard personnel expenses related to the 2005 hurricanes. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The reference to a congressional budget resolution and the emergency designation stays entirely inside the federal government, so it is not participation.
opus.s: For an additional amount for “National Guard Personnel, Army”, $1,304,000, for necessary expenses related to the consequences of Hurricane Katrina and other hurricanes of the 2005 season

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple appropriation authorization and emergency designation. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, or the public) in the decision-making process. The text only specifies the amount, purpose, and legal classification of the funds.
qwen_chat.s: For an additional amount for “National Guard Personnel, Army”, $1,304,000, for necessary expenses related to the consequences of Hurricane Katrina and other hurricanes of the 2005 season: Provided, That the amount provided under this heading is designated as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 402 of H. Con. Res. 95 (109th Congress), the concurrent resolution on the budget for fiscal year 2006.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for "consequences of Hurricane Katrina," there is an implicit need for coordination with local governments or victims. However, the text itself only authorizes an appropriation and designates it as an emergency requirement. It does not mandate any specific consultation, hearing, or participation process with outside parties. The definition requires explicit involvement of outside parties in the decision-making process (e.g., advisory boards, comment periods, consultation requirements). Mere funding authorization without procedural mandates for outside input is not participation.
